principles: Every released requirement, allocation, derived input, characteristic, CAD binding, process, drawing and inspection plan has a revision/effectivity statement.
A characteristic revision states which part/configuration revision or engineering baseline it applies to and which predecessor it supersedes, if any.
Changing a characteristic does not rewrite historical released revisions; a successor revision is created and downstream consumers become stale according to effectivity.
Design-review candidates may be baseline-scoped before a formal part revision exists, but release is blocked while release effectivity is OPEN.
As-built/as-inspected results retain the exact released definition fingerprint/revision used for that unit or lot.
